question:
The below given image is of which of the following animal?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a95c381d17f1365a0e8ff37ff704f13cc5ca6ac0af40f53caad0c7a08d67848.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nilgiri Tahr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Nilgiri Tahr** (*Nilgiritragus hylocrius*) is an endemic species found in the **Western Ghats** of India, particularly in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

• This animal is a type of **mountain goat** known for its unique appearance, with a coarse, short fur coat that is usually brown or gray and a distinctive curved horn.

• The Nilgiri Tahr is the **state animal of Tamil Nadu** and is listed as **Endangered** under the IUCN Red List due to habitat loss and poaching.

• They are typically found in rugged terrains and grasslands at altitudes of 1,200-2,600 meters, such as the Eravikulam National Park and the Mukurthi National Park.

• Unlike other species of Tahr, the Nilgiri Tahr prefers open terrain and is known for its excellent climbing skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Barasingha:** 

• The Barasingha (*Rucervus duvaucelii*), also known as the swamp deer, is found in the marshy grasslands of northern and central India, including regions like Assam, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.

• It is recognized by its large antlers that can have up to 12 tines or points.

• The Barasingha is listed as **Vulnerable** under the IUCN Red List due to habitat destruction and poaching.

• **Sambar Deer:** 

• The Sambar deer (*Rusa unicolor*) is one of the largest deer species and is native to the Indian subcontinent.

• It has a thick coat of brown fur and large, rugged antlers. It is commonly found in dense forests and grasslands.

• This species is listed as **Vulnerable** in the IUCN Red List but is widely distributed across India.

• **Chital:** 

• The Chital (*Axis axis*), also known as the spotted deer, is one of the most commonly seen deer species in India.

• It is recognized by its reddish-brown coat with white spots and is found in open grasslands and deciduous forests.

• The Chital is listed as **Least Concern** under the IUCN Red List due to its wide distribution and stable population.

• **Conservation Efforts for Nilgiri Tahr:** 

• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is protected under **Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, which ensures the highest level of protection under Indian law.

• Efforts like habitat restoration and anti-poaching measures are being implemented in areas like the **Eravikulam National Park** to protect this species.

• State governments, along with wildlife organizations, regularly conduct population surveys and awareness programs to ensure the long-term survival of the species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The Nilgiri Tahr is one of the few species of mountain goats found in South India and is an important part of the ecosystem in the Western Ghats.

• Its conservation status highlights the critical need for preserving biodiversity hotspots like the Western Ghats, which are under threat from deforestation and human encroachment.

• Tourism in areas like the Eravikulam National Park has raised awareness about the Nilgiri Tahr but has also led to challenges in balancing conservation with human activities.

• Programs like the **Nilgiri Tahr Conservation Project** aim to mitigate the threats faced by this species and ensure its survival for future generations.
